title: Lodha Developers Ltd - 543287 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Lodha FY26 presales INR205bn (+16%) and PAT INR34.3bn (20% margin); FY27 presales guided to INR240bn, PAT growth ~20% medium term.
summary.overview: Lodha delivered its best-ever quarter in Q4 FY26 with presales of about INR58.9bn (+23% YoY), and full-year presales of INR205bn (+16%) with every quarter a record. PAT grew 24% to INR34.3bn, with PAT margin touching 20% for the first time, while adjusted EBITDA grew 14% and the embedded development margin held near 33%. Management shifted its primary guidance metric to PAT, guiding FY27 presales of about INR240bn (mid-teens growth) and PAT growth of about 20% CAGR to over INR85bn by FY31. Business development was strong, with 12 projects and INR600bn GDV added, and net debt fell to 0.23x equity.

segments.name: South & Central Mumbai
segments.commentary: Growing at 25%+ CAGR; branded developer share in the INR400bn+ market rose from about 30% to 40%. Sewri cited as emerging hotspot with 5x growth.

segments.name: Luxury (INR50cr+ / INR100cr+)
segments.commentary: Company holds 40% share of the INR100cr+ segment and leads South & Central by sales with about 30% CAGR since FY23; INR50cr+ projects realise 30% higher per sq ft price.

segments.name: Bengaluru
segments.commentary: Contributed about INR24bn presales in FY26, over 12% of total, three years after pilot entry in FY23.

segments.name: Palava / Extended Eastern suburbs
segments.commentary: Q4 Palava presales near INR800cr; extended eastern suburbs sales flat at INR20-25bn for four years; average Palava price about INR11,000/sq ft carpet vs INR20,000+ in Airoli and INR25,000+ in Mulund/Thane.

segments.name: Annuity / RentCo (retail, office, warehousing)
segments.commentary: Annuity income about INR3bn in FY26 from 3.8mn sq ft complete of 8.8mn sq ft pipeline; target about INR10bn annual rent by FY31 excluding data centres.

segments.name: Data centres (Palava green DC park)
segments.commentary: 400 acres shovel-ready; AWS and STT secured as anchors; plan about 1GW powered shell on 100 acres, incremental cost INR100-110bn, income expected from FY29.

guidance_outlook: FY27 presales guidance of about INR240bn, with embedded EBITDA margin of 32-34%, including single-digit % land sales contribution.
FY27 launch pipeline of INR218bn GDV identified; NCR launches (2 JDA projects, Gurgaon, GDV about INR33bn) excluded and expected Q4 FY27 or early FY28.
First-half FY27 presales expected in low 40s % of full-year guidance; assumes Middle East situation normalises by end of Q1 FY27.
OCF to grow about 20% p.a. from INR71bn base, in line with PAT growth; no separate OCF guidance given.
Medium-term PAT CAGR of about 20%, from INR34bn in FY26 to over INR85bn by FY31.
Price growth expected about 5% and volume growth 11-12% (sq ft) in FY27.
Average DevCo to become debt-free over next few years; total debt at end FY27 expected lower than FY26 despite annuity capex.
capex_capacity: Available GDV for sale about INR2trn as of 1 April 2026, excluding long-term township land not used in next 5 years; business development capex to be meaningfully reduced over next 2 years.
Business development: 12 projects, INR600bn GDV added in FY26 (2.4x own guidance).

Data centre: about 1GW powered shell on 100 of 400 acres, incremental cost INR100-110bn largely self-funded from land sales; land value at STT transaction INR210-230mn per acre; ~30% of US/EU power shell construction cost.
Annuity pipeline 8.8mn sq ft, of which 3.8mn sq ft complete; LandCo created for monetisation of 3,900-acre Extended Eastern suburbs land (about 600mn sq ft potential).
Mulund-Airoli-Palava freeway expected in 2-3 months; Thane portion of Mumbai-Nagpur expressway targeted before Diwali; Palava bullet train station targeted 2028-29.
demand_pricing: Macro: management flagged March deferral of closures amid Middle East tensions, with shortfalls from NRI buyers in the Middle East and in luxury closures; sees housing as a relative beneficiary.

Construction cost impact of 3-5% of construction cost, concentrated in gas-linked items (tiles, paints, PVC, aluminium formwork); estimated margin impact about 0.35% of sales over 6 months, or about 1.7% if persistent over 3 years.
Labour attrition running 5-10% above seasonal norms in March-April.
Median Lodha buyer household income about INR50 lakh p.a.; entry-level about INR25 lakh.
Market: 3-4 bed segment growing 15-20% CAGR vs about 4% for sub-3 bed; 3-4 bed price growth double-digit vs 6% overall market. INR50cr+ share of market rose from 7% to 13% since FY24.

qa_highlights.question: Will FCF turn positive through lower capex and OCF growth, and why is there no OCF guidance for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Business development investment to be muted over 2 years given visibility; OCF expected to grow about 20% p.a. from INR71bn in line with PAT, with other linked factors not separately guided.

qa_highlights.question: How ready is the FY27 INR218bn launch pipeline and what is the status of environmental clearances?
qa_highlights.answer: New launches were about one-third of FY26 sales and will be slightly lower in FY27; all projects have land acquired, designs done and approvals available or in process. Management said the environmental clearance issue (Supreme Court order August 2025) is behind the market, with clearances resuming from November 2025.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for data centre build-to-suit announcements and lease income?
qa_highlights.answer: Advanced discussions on first BTS boxes; announcements expected this fiscal; lease income expected from FY29, about two years after signing.

qa_highlights.question: Which segments were hit by Middle East disruption and what is April trend?
qa_highlights.answer: March shortfalls were in NRI sales from the Middle East and luxury closures; no persistent segment impact expected. Management did not give April trend, expects H1 growth around 15%.

qa_highlights.question: Palava residential outlook for FY27 with road infrastructure completion?
qa_highlights.answer: Expects presales growth in the Extended Eastern suburbs to exceed company-level growth in FY27, with timing dependent on freeway and Thane highway openings; no number given.

qa_highlights.question: Cost inflation impact and labour attrition?
qa_highlights.answer: Construction cost up 3-5%, margin impact nominal; labour attrition 5-10% above seasonal norms, viewed as manageable.

qa_highlights.question: Own data centre vs monetising land?
qa_highlights.answer: About 100 of 400 acres to be used for own portfolio, rest sold; strategic decision to build long-term annuity income using land sale proceeds.

qa_highlights.question: Will leverage fall in FY27 given strong FCF?
qa_highlights.answer: DevCo may become net debt zero over next few years; overall debt at end FY27 expected to be somewhat lower than FY26 despite annuity build-out.

risks_watch: Middle East escalation: guidance assumes normalisation by end of Q1 FY27; persistent energy shock could delay closures and raise costs.
Construction cost and labour: gas-linked material inflation and 5-10% excess labour attrition.
Extended Eastern suburbs ramp depends on freeway and Thane highway timelines; management already deferred about 12 months.
Unsold inventory elevated at FY26 end after deferred Q4 launches; management says conversion not expected to fall.
Back-ended sales: H1 FY27 expected in low 40s % of guidance, so H2 delivery critical.
Land monetisation plan (LandCo) and data centre timelines to be updated at next annual call.
summary.management_tone: Confident and strategically framed on long-term PAT, cash flow and annuity build-out; more cautious on near-term sales, acknowledging March deferrals and Middle East uncertainty, and reluctant to give precise timing on data centre and Palava sales.
key_quotes: Net debt, which stood at 3.5x equity at IPO, is now at 0. 23x. We have grown at scale while simultaneously deleveraging.
For us, the presales are a means to an end. The end is ultimately profitability, and that's what our focus is.
Our guidance for FY '27, we are guiding to presales of about INR240 billion with an embedded EBITDA margin of 32% to 34%.
